title: Shannon entropy
summary: Entropy is the expected self-information of a random variable's distribution.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared discrete information theory context is fixed.

content.plain: Entropy is the expected self-information of a random variable's distribution.
content.exact: For discrete X with probabilities p(x), H_b(X)=−Σ_x p(x)log_b p(x), with 0log0 interpreted as 0.
content.example: A fair bit has entropy 1 bit; a deterministic bit has entropy 0.
content.caveat: Shannon entropy is distribution-relative and does not measure semantic importance.
